topology: Four routers in a compact U layout: R1/R2 area0, R2/R3 normal transit area10, R3/R4 area20. PC1 is on the R1 core LAN, PC2 on the R2 local control LAN, and SRV1 on the R4 remote service LAN. Initial physical neighbors are Full but reciprocal router-ID virtual links are missing. Intended links use matching MD5 key1 and default virtual Hello10/Dead40; physical transits cost10 and passive host LANs1.
implemented: Twenty-fourth ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry, independent practice/reference documents, seven-row addressing/role plan, staged guide, ordinary verified IOS/Windows commands and shareable current-origin/path/query permalink. Existing icons, theme, terminal styling, layout and offline delivery are preserved.

Reciprocal area10 virtual-link peer router IDs2.2.2.2/3.3.3.3, explicit message-digest authentication and matching Virtual10 key1 restore computed logical backbone continuity. Virtual-link UP depends on reciprocal configuration and received normal-transit OSPF topology; actual protocol89 filtering withdraws the underlay and routes.

Reference learns remote service/core LANs as O IA AD110/metric31 at R1/R4, service as IA21 at R2 and core as intra-area O21 at R3. Request forwarding uses actual physical next hops R1-R2-R3-R4, without synthetic data tunnels. Received area10 summary inspection identifies R3 as service advertiser and R2 as core advertiser.

Initial diagnosis and six controlled exercises distinguish wrong interface-IP peer identity, missing reciprocal configuration, virtual Hello mismatch, mismatched MD5 key, passive physical transit and real backbone attachment loss. Local PC2/R2 traffic stays operational. During passive transit, direct R2/R3 IP probes still work; physical OSPF and the logical virtual link fail. Backbone loss is graded by withdrawn core/service routes and traffic, independently of whether a virtual adjacency remains up.

Each success requires three unique original requests accepted at the destination, parent-correlated replies and expected physical router egresses. Failure requires actual No route drops correlated to original requests or their replies, with independent working controls. Config/RIB epochs reject stale, partial and configuration-only proof. HTTP requires complete TCP-backed PC1/SRV1 response and actual four-router egress.

Seven live checks cover policy, physical peers, logical virtual links, routes, database, health and saved configuration. Nine observed checks cover initial diagnosis, four traffic directions, completed HTTP and six incidents. Practice0/16, diagnosis1/16, repaired baseline10/16, full16/16; reference only seven live goals. YAML retains earned history and rebuilds runtime.

Fixed decimal/dotted transit-area alias identity so update/removal targets one link and preserves unrelated options. Improved show ip ospf virtual-links to display configured peer, derived up/down, actual transit interface/cost, configured timers and authentication/key ID without secrets or invented timers/uptime/counters. Physical-neighbor display stays separate, as in the cited Cisco example.
scope: IOS OSPFv2 logical virtual-link configuration, received physical transit topology, computed backbone SPF and actual simulated packet forwarding. The existing engine exchanges segmented logical router records; virtual adjacency is derived rather than a separate virtual wire Hello/DBD FSM. It does not encode individual virtual area0 router-LSA links, implement DoNotAge/demand-circuit flooding, calculate cryptographic wire MD5 digests or claim full RFC timing/interoperability. Database grading inspects existing received area10 summaries rather than inventing virtual area0 LSAs. No fresh CML capture is claimed.
